_note: First ISx-JAX run, 2026-08-14, 4x TPU v5e (v5litepod-4, 2x2) in us-west4-a via GKE Autopilot. Verification PASSED. This is an untuned baseline and the rate is NOT a fabric measurement; see _analysis.

_analysis.headline: The network is not the bottleneck, which is the opposite of what ISx is designed to show.
_analysis.evidence: Probe B measured jax.lax.all_to_all on uint64 at 175 GB/s off-chip on this same hardware. This end-to-end run reports 0.20 GB/s. The exchange is therefore well under 1% of the 673 ms, and the remaining time is local work.
_analysis.cause: The padded exchange costs two full sorts per iteration. build_padded() argsorts all 4.19M local keys to group them by destination, then jax.lax.sort runs again over the 5.45M-slot padded receive buffer. XLA needs static shapes, so the destination-major layout is built with an argsort plus a scatter rather than the counting pass the C version uses.
not_yet_tried: ragged_all_to_all, which this JAX has, removing the 30% padding and one of the sorts
a radix pass instead of argsort for the local bucketing, matching src/isx64
larger keys-per-device, since 0.13 GB total is far too small to saturate ICI
_analysis.fair_comparison_warning: Do not quote 0.20 GB/s against the H4D path. It measures an untuned local phase on a 0.13 GB problem, not the TPU interconnect.
